title: Lateral topic holdout embed probe benchmark
content:
Purpose:
This is a working benchmark and data curation guide for a targeted embeddings regression suite focused on: lateral-topic holdouts, short-to-long query mismatch, and realistic noise that breaks clustering. The goal is a compact, reproducible probe bank that complements our larger embedsets: fast to run in CI, representative of production failure modes, and informative for both semantic search and clustering stability.

Scope and intended use:
- Use during model onboarding (before promotion to hosted catalog) and as part of nightly regression for quantized/optimized kernels.
- Focuses on 6 languages: en, es, fr, pt, de, zh (simplified).
- Covers three workload axes: topical holdouts (lateral/generalization), query length mismatch (short->long), and adversarial/noise perturbations.
- Not a full production embedset; designed for quick signal (<=10k corpus, <=2k queries).

High-level dataset composition (target sizes):
- Base corpus: 8,000 documents across domains (docs: documentation, product reviews, news, forum threads, legal snippets, code comments).
- Topic holdouts: 20 holdout topics, each with ~150 in-domain docs and 25 lateral-topic docs (dev/test split).
- Query bank: 2,000 queries (balanced by language and query style).
- Cluster probes: 500 cluster sanity groups (varying sizes 3-20) with controlled noise insertions.

Sampling methodology:
1) Topic selection: pick 20 medium-granularity topics (e.g., "privacy policy changes", "battery degradation patterns", "refund dispute workflows") that appear across domains. For each topic construct: seed doc set, near-topic distractors, and lateral topics (intuitively related but distinct).
2) Lateral holdout split: for each topic, hold out a contiguous subset of seed documents from the corpus (20%) as the "lateral" test pool. Lateral queries are designed to probe generalization from related wording.
3) Query generation: mix of human-written and model-augmented queries. Start from 3 human prompts per topic (short keyword, user question, long intent-rich paragraph). Use augmentation (paraphrase model) to expand to 50 queries per topic, then manually sample to keep diversity.
4) Noise modes: typo insertion (char swap, missing char), extreme truncation (suffix/prefix keep), paraphrase drift, language-mismatch snippets (code + English), boilerplate duplication. Insert noise at controlled rates (10% light, 5% heavy) for cluster probes.

Annotation protocol (relevance labels and cluster flags):
- Relevance labels (for retrieval/semantic-search pairs): 0 = unrelated, 1 = tangential, 2 = related, 3 = exact/relevant answer.
- Cluster membership: gold cluster id for grouping. Annotators mark whether item is a clean member, borderline, or noisy insertion.
- Instructions highlights: label highest-ranking short snippet that would answer an explicit user question; prefer higher precision on fine-grained topics; when in doubt mark borderline.
- Inter-annotator agreement: run a 200-pair qualification set; require Cohen's kappa >= 0.6 before accepting annotations.

Clustering sanity checks and probes:
- Silhouette drift test: compute silhouette scores per cluster and compare to baseline model; flag >0.08 drop.
- Anchor stability: pick 50 random anchors (one per topic). For each anchor, list top-10 NN and compute overlap with baseline top-10. Alert if mean overlap < 0.5.
- Quiet cluster detection: clusters with expected coherence (topic) but high intra-cluster variance — surface for manual review.
- Noise sensitivity: measure cluster purity as noise insertions increase; expected graceful degradation curve defined below.

Metrics and thresholds (CI-focused):
- Retrieval: MRR@10, Recall@10, NDCG@10 per-language and averaged. Regression alert if MRR@10 drops by >3% absolute or >7% relative vs baseline.
- Clustering: mean silhouette, cluster purity@k. Alert if silhouette drops by >0.08 or purity drops by >6 percentage points.
- Similarity distribution shift: compare cosine similarity percentile shifts between positive pairs; alert if 10th percentile of positives drops >0.05.
- Anchor overlap: mean top-10 overlap < 0.5 triggers investigation.

Quick CI smoke checklist (what to run locally before filing a regression):
- Run: python eval/run_lateral_bench.py --model <path> --corpus data/lateral_corpus.json --queries queries/lateral_queries.json --out results.json
- Inspect results.json: top-level metrics, per-language breakdown, sample failure pairs for the 3 worst topics.
- Run clustering probe: python eval/cluster_probes.py --embeds results.emb --clusters gold_clusters.json --report cluster_report.md
- Add at least 5 manually inspected pairs in PR description when opening a regression ticket.

Example CLI and expected output snippets (pseudo):
- python eval/run_lateral_bench.py --model models/v1 --corpus lateral_corpus.json --queries lateral_queries.json
  => metrics: MRR@10: 0.421 (baseline 0.439), Recall@10: 0.732 (baseline 0.748)
- python eval/anchor_check.py --embeds v1.emb --anchors anchors.json
  => anchor_overlap_mean: 0.46 (ALERT), worst_topic: "refund dispute workflows" overlap 0.2

Example query/document triplets (for clarity):
- Query (en, short): "battery swelling causes"
  Gold doc excerpt: "long-term degradation and swelling observed in Li-ion cells under high-charge cycles" (label=3)
- Query (es, long): "¿por qué mi teléfono se sobrecalienta después de usar la cámara durante varios minutos?"
  Gold doc excerpt: "cámara y SoC térmicos: interacción entre procesamiento de imagen y throttling" (label=2)
- Cluster probe example: cluster_id=42 contains forum posts about "refund timing"; injected noise: duplicate auto-reply email snip. Annotator label: noisy insertion.

Regression triage playbook (short):
1) Reproduce locally with the bench and check per-language deltas.
2) If signal localized to quantization/ops change, run fp16 vs quantized kernels with same weights.
3) Check tokenization artifacts (multilingual mismatch), especially for zh and mixed code+text.
4) Generate top-20 NN for 10 anchors and save in /tmp/anchor_debug; attach to ticket.
5) If clustering degradation present, pull cluster_report.md and a 50-sample manual review.

Open questions and decisions needed before this becomes canonical:
- Should we include more low-resource languages (e.g., hi, ar) for edge-case coverage, or keep bench small? Tradeoff: cost vs signal.
- What is the official baseline model (v1) we freeze for the next 6 months? Recommend: models/emb-v2-fp16 as interim.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Finalize 20 topic list and seed doc pulls (owner: Marco) by 2024-10-05
- [ ] Produce human-written seed queries and run augmentation (owner: Lin) by 2024-10-18
- [ ] Run annotation qualification and onboard 3 annotators (owner: Priya) by 2024-11-01
- [ ] Wire CI job and alert thresholds (owner: Aisha) by 2024-11-15

Notes / context:
- This doc intentionally keeps the benchmark compact so it is suitable for both pre-release gating and nightly checks. It is complementary to our larger embedsets (semantic-search-large, multilingual-curation) but focuses on lateral generalization and cluster brittleness which are frequent regression sources in quantized builds.

Contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) for bench design questions and CI wiring.
